newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish Protestants blamed for Catholic's murder.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish Protestants blamed for Catholic's murder.

text.p: British security sources blamed banned Protestant guerrillas on Friday for the murder of a Catholic shot in his home in an Irish nationalist area of West Belfast a week ago, BBC radio reported.

The shooting, which raised fears of a new round of "tit-for-tat" sectarian killing in Northern Ireland, was not claimed by any group but the sources told the BBC they now believed members of the pro-British Ulster Freedom Fighters shot John Slane.

It is one of four groups in the outlawed Combined Loyalist Military Command (CLMC) which called a truce in October 1994 in a bitter conflict with Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas fighting to end British rule.
Loyalist hardliners have been blamed for five attacks on Catholics since December when the IRA stepped up armed hostilities against British forces.
"I have spoken to a number of security sources who now believe that elements of the UFF murdered Mr Slane," reported Brian Rowan, BBC Northern Ireland's chief security correspondent.
Loyalist sources close to the organisation continued to deny knowledge of the murder, but that fitted with a pattern of unclaimed breaches of the ceasefire, he added.
Britain regards the Loyalist ceasefire as shaky but still in operation. Loyalist parties with seats in multi-party talks insist it is in force.

The IRA's Sinn Fein political arm brands the Loyalist ceasefire a sham. Sinn Fein accuses Britain of double standards for denying it a place at the talks until the IRA, which has killed two soldiers in six months, abandons violence.
Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams accused political leaders of virtually ignoring Slane's murder.

"There is a very wide widespread anger in West Belfast about the silence of the political establishment both in Dublin and here about this killing. One week after his death, John Slane's killing is being treated by many politicians as if it never happened," he said in a statement.
